case.case_title: Dissanayake, Attorney-at-Law on Behalf of K.M. Lai v. Sujeewa, Sub Inspector of Police, Meetiyagoda Police Station and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1998) 2 Sri L.R. 413

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the detention of the petitioner was lawful and complied with the requirement to bring the detainee before a judge and have a legal order for detention under Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was detained unlawfully without being brought before a judge or having a legal order authorizing his detention.
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents claimed the petitioner was arrested lawfully on complaint and released on bail after hospital admission, implying lawful detention.
key_facts: Petitioner was taken to police station and later admitted to hospital unconscious.
Petitioner was not allowed visitors at police station and was transferred between hospitals.
Petitioner was released on bail on 03.06.1996 after hospital admission.
Court found arrest and detention unlawful and violative of Article 13(2).

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained must be brought before a judge and cannot be held without a legal order. The court emphasized the necessity of judicial oversight to prevent unlawful detention.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the petitioner was detained unlawfully without being brought before a judge or having a legal order. The detention was therefore in violation of Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention without judicial order or bringing detainee before a judge is unlawful.
Judicial oversight is essential to protect fundamental rights against unlawful detention.
Violation of Article 13(2) constitutes infringement of fundamental rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that the detention of the petitioner violated Article 13(2) of the Constitution as he was not brought before a judge and was held without legal order.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Same compensation and costs as for Article 13(1) violation.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner’s detention was unlawful because he was not brought before a judge and held without legal order, violating his fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was detained at the police station and hospitals without being brought before a judge or having a legal order, and was not allowed visitors at the police station.
